title: [Proposal] Add an additional APAC collector/agent SIG
body:
Apologies if I have opened this in the wrong spot, please feel free move it into the correct place.

I am looking for an expression of interesting in running an additional meeting for those working in APAC and wanting to actively contribute back to the project.

Looking at the otel calendar,  4:00pm Pacific (Taken from the otel Instrumetation APAC SIG) works well for me. 

Or roughly -22:00 UTC through to +08:00 UTC (negative being the previous day respective to UTC)

comments.body:
Discussed in the Feb 1 SIG call, the proposal is to add 2 meetings to the calendar:

- 1st Wednesday is EU-APAC friendly
- 3rd Wednesday is NA-APAC friendly

Here is one table with proposed and existing **starting** meeting times at some relevant timezones (US West Coast, US East Coast, CET which covers most of Europe, China, and Sidney):

|         | UTC−08:00 (PST) | UTC -05:00 (EST) | UTC +01:00 (CET) | UTC +08:00 (China) | UTC +10:00 (Sidney) |

| EU-APAC | *00:00*         | *03:00*          | **09:00**            | **16:00**              | **19:00**               |
| NA-APAC | **16:00**           | **19:00**            | *01:00*          | **08:00**              | **11:00**               |

I think the 08:00 UTC to 09:00 UTC is the most reasonable one, the only other possibility would maybe be 07:00 UTC to 08:00 UTC (but it's IMO too early for a meeting on the UK/Ireland, where we also have had some contributors).

Any alternative proposals? Do these times make sense?

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
TL;DR; this was implicitly rolled back into a second/review session of the existing time slot, then canceled. There's some interest in a 3 timezone proposal. We want UTC+8 to be able to attend in normal working hours, and 8am is acceptable. Let's bring it back as a meeting of peers, not a review session of decisions made by other regions.

---

What was proposed here eventually turned into a second meeting on the same day as the primary one, and eventually canceled. This seems in hindsight an unsurprising end as there's no incentive to join, as review meetings don't lead to impact or maintainer, etc (my opinion). It ends up a predictable road towards cancelation and this has happened outside CNCF also.

There's a resurgence of interest, but specifically that a meeting friendly to UTC+8 is a primary meeting, not a review meeting. That way, it doesn't end up being canceled from lack of purpose as we all can just watch videos. The idea is to better leverage timezones like this one, which have >20pct of the earth's population. We should be able to grow the community in a way that also doesn't require one part of the earth to be watchers, or have to miss sleep or family requirements.

Initially, this was a request to make two times, the existing unfriendly to APAC one and a second primary meeting 8am UTC+8. This is specifically 8am not 7am as existing contributors have family responsibilities. 8am is a good choice as it is extremely friendly to west coast US canada etc, at 4pm. This overlap is important to make the meeting sustainable. The agenda should be exclusive topics not simply rehash or study session. To get quorum we need to begin by folks sharing their influence, by presenting topics in the UTC+8 friendly time. Once more contributors grow there will both be a point proven (we desire to and did grow the community) and the region becomes more self-sufficient and equals with others. 

We *must* do everything we can to avoid the well worn track of setting this up for failure. If we only make this a study session of other timezones, or are impatient to quickly cancel, or folks in west coast don't attend at all, basically it is our fault, not the fault of the region that this failed. Let's not do that.

Later, there was interest in.. well, let's also recognize that if we do 50/50 2 meetings, it is very unbalanced vs today. Some people would like to attend more discussions and 8am UTC+8 is very unfriendly to europe. So, instead of them going from 100% content to 50%, to step down more gracefully to 2/3.. via a 3 meeting system. I believe this is an earnest interest in making sure this is viable and again not a path to canceling UTC+8 again. So, personally, sounds fine.

comments.body:
Here's an initial proposal for the time slots. Note that locations on CEST, BST, EDT, and PDT will be shifted by one hour (earlier) for parts of the year.

Even splitting into three slots, I have challenges accommodating all time zones for at least two slots. For instance, the following ones have only one slot between 08:00 and 18:00 local times: Brasilia (slot 1), New York (slot 1), Delhi (slot 3). That said, I think it's a good start and worth trying.

EDIT(2024-07-03): after the discussion on 3 July 2024 during the Collector SIG, we agreed to change the proposal, so that we have two slots for Brazil, New York, and Delhi, and one for Beijing. This should accommodate a good number of existing contributors, while still being an improvement for Beijing.

Slot 1: NASA/EMEA, 16:00 UTC (current slot)
* 18:00 Berlin (CEST)
* 17:00 London (BST)
* 13:00 Brasilia
* 12:00 New York (EDT)
* 09:00 San Francisco (PDT)
* 00:00 Beijing
* 21:30 Delhi

Slot 2: NASA/APAC, 00:00 UTC
* 02:00 Berlin
* 01:00 London
* 21:00 Brasilia
* 20:00 New York
* 17:00 San Francisco
* 08:00 Beijing
* 05:30 Delhi

Slot 3: EMEA/APAC, 12:00 UTC
* 14:00 Berlin
* 13:00 London
* 09:00 Brasilia
* 08:00 New York
* 05:00 San Francisco
* 20:00 Beijing
* 17:30 Delhi

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Expanding from @participant5 comment: we still have the EMEA-APAC meeting happening monthly at 9am CEST. Some notes about the experience there:
- Average attendance is about 1-2 people and (most of the time) @participant6 and me
- We frequently have to postpone decisions to the usual meeting time and rely stuff on people's behalf

The fact that it doesn't work great is not necessarily an argument against restoring the NASA-APAC meeting, we may have not publicized the new meeting times well enough and we may not have a sufficiently well-defined decision process, these are both things we can address

comments.author: codeboten
comments.body:
Discussed in 03-Jul-2024 SIG call, it would be great to capture some details as to how decisions can be made through ad-hoc meetings when synchronous discussions are needed as maintainers/approvers may not be able to attend the split meetings.

I really like the idea of making this community more inclusive to other timezones. I'd also propose we run this as an experiment for a set amount of time (3/6 months) to validate that the new split meetings are working to continue to move the project forward. After which we can review community engagement to ensure it is continuing to foster the collaboration that is needed.

There was an attempt to do this in the Python community many years ago and we saw a drop in engagement because of the split. This is why I'm suggesting we schedule a time to review engagement.

comments.author: participant7
comments.body: Thank you all for taking a look into this, it would be great if the larger community can profit from your experience after those 3-6 months as well, e.g. via https://github.com/open-telemetry/community/issues/2176
